## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

# Death Data Maps

 For Everyone 

Apr. 15, 2026, visit link for details.

## Key points

*   The National Vital Statistics System provides a range of death-related statistics based on data from death certificates.
*   Find U.S. maps with state and District of Columbia data for 17 causes of death, including chronic diseases, infectious diseases, and injuries.
*   A map of state-level infant death data also is available.   

![Image 6: An icon of a  gravestone that depicts leading cause of death](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/media/images/2025/07/NCHS_SoS_death_1200x675.png)


## Leading causes of death

The [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) (NVSS) receives, analyzes, and shares data about deaths across the nation. NVSS experts use these data to determine the leading causes of death—the diseases, injuries, and other causes that lead to the most deaths each year.

Stats of the States provides U.S. maps featuring state-level data for 17 of the most common causes of death.

# Death Data Maps

 For Everyone 

Apr. 15, 2026, visit link for details.

## Key points

*   The National Vital Statistics System provides a range of death-related statistics based on data from death certificates.
*   Find U.S. maps with state and District of Columbia data for 17 causes of death, including chronic diseases, infectious diseases, and injuries.
*   A map of state-level infant death data also is available.   

![Image 6: An icon of a  gravestone that depicts leading cause of death](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/media/images/2025/07/NCHS_SoS_death_1200x675.png)


## Leading causes of death

The [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) (NVSS) receives, analyzes, and shares data about deaths across the nation. NVSS experts use these data to determine the leading causes of death—the diseases, injuries, and other causes that lead to the most deaths each year.

Stats of the States provides U.S. maps featuring state-level data for 17 of the most common causes of death.
